card.name: Prepositions of where to inject or apply
card.fires_on: The small place words 'into', 'onto', 'on' or 'in' right after an administering or applying verb, often after 'directly', 'rather than' or 'not'. They introduce the body site or surface that receives the drug.

modes.label: After 'directly'
modes.description: Place word following 'directly' in instructions about where to inject or dispense.
modes.example: Avoid inadvertent injection directly<< into>> an artery or a vein as it can

modes.label: Contrast with the right site
modes.description: Place word after 'rather than' or 'not' naming a site to avoid.
modes.example: Injections should be made into the affected tendon sheaths rather than<< into>> the tendons themselves.

modes.label: Plain site after a dose
modes.description: Place word after a verb or dose phrase leading to the target site.
modes.example: One drop<< into>> the affected eye(s) once daily in
